description: ITEM 1 (HIGHEST PRIORITY): Fix cloud/local API-key persistence. TRACED ROOT CAUSE: crates/secrets/Cargo.toml declares `keyring = "3"` with NO features. keyring v3 has NO default features and REQUIRES an explicit platform-store feature (windows-native / apple-native / a secret-service feature); with none enabled it silently uses the platform-independent MOCK/no-op credential store. On the user's Windows build, KeyringSecretStore::store therefore writes to a volatile mock that does NOT persist to Windows Credential Manager, so at enumeration time / next launch resolve finds nothing -> exactly 'auth error: no secret found for handle gemini-cloud' / 'generic-openai-local'. The store paths in commands.rs already propagate store() errors via `?`, so the mock silently accepting the write (never erroring) is why the UI showed 'saved' while nothing persisted. FIX: enable the correct per-target keyring backend feature; make any keychain store/resolve failure visible; add a user-triggerable keychain self-test so the user's Windows build definitively reports keychain health (we cannot exercise a real keychain in the sandbox). Add unit tests for InMemory + store-error propagation.
steps: In crates/secrets/Cargo.toml, replace `keyring = "3"` with a target-conditional dependency that enables the platform-native backend feature per OS: Windows -> `windows-native`, macOS/iOS -> `apple-native`, Linux/BSD -> an appropriate secret-service feature (e.g. `sync-secret-service` with a rustls or openssl crypto feature, matching what keyring v3 requires; pick the vendored/rustls variant to avoid a system openssl dependency in CI). Use `[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies]` / `[target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")'...]` / `[target.'cfg(...linux...)'...]` blocks (or the `cfg` table form) so each platform pulls keyring with `default-features = false, features = [<backend>]`. Keep the version pinned at 3 and keep the manifest self-contained (this crate is [workspace] exclude; no workspace inheritance). Update the manifest's existing rationale comment to explain WHY the backend feature is mandatory (keyring v3 has no default store; without a platform feature it uses a mock/no-op store that does not persist - the exact v0.8.1 bug).

Confirm the crate still declares its deps such that CI's standalone `cargo build/test --manifest-path crates/secrets/Cargo.toml` on ubuntu resolves: the Linux secret-service backend must build on the CI runner (headless), and the automated tests must still use InMemorySecretStore only (keep the keyring round-trip test #[ignore]d). If the Linux secret-service backend would require a system libdbus at build time on CI, prefer the keyutils-based `linux-native` feature (builds without a running Secret Service) OR guard so CI still compiles; document the choice in the manifest comment.

In crates/secrets/src/lib.rs, add a self-test method to the SecretStore surface usable for a health check WITHOUT weakening the resolve-is-the-only-plaintext-seam invariant: add a `fn self_test(&self) -> Result<(), SecretError>` (default trait method) that stores a fixed sentinel value under a dedicated temp handle (e.g. 'harbor-selftest'), resolves it, asserts round-trip equality, then deletes it - returning Ok on success and a display-safe SecretError on any mismatch/failure. It must NOT return the sentinel across its signature (returns `Result<(), SecretError>`), preserving the no-plaintext-accessor invariant. Add a unit test over InMemorySecretStore proving self_test() returns Ok, and a test proving a store that fails round-trip yields Err (use a small test-only failing store or assert the mismatch path).

Add a store-error-propagation unit test: build a test-only SecretStore whose store() returns Err, and assert that set_cloud_provider_inner / set_local_runtime_inner surface that Err as a CommandError rather than persisting a ProviderConfig row (verify no row is written on store failure). If the existing code already inserts the row before/after store, confirm ordering makes store() failure abort BEFORE the ProviderConfig upsert; if not, reorder so the secret is stored FIRST and a store failure prevents the config row from being written (a config row pointing at a non-existent secret is exactly the 'no secret found' symptom). Keep the change minimal and covered by the test.

Add a display-safe Tauri command `test_key_storage` (rename_all camelCase) in crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs that calls state.secret_store.self_test() and returns a small view like `{ ok: bool, detail: String }` (detail is display-safe, never secret material). Register it in generate_handler! in crates/tauri-app/src/lib.rs. Add the typed IPC wrapper in frontend/src/ipc/commands.ts and its TS return type in frontend/src/types/index.ts (camelCase).

Surface the self-test in the Settings Diagnostics section (frontend/src/features/settings/DiagnosticsSection.tsx): add a 'Test key storage' button that invokes test_key_storage and renders the ok/detail result (harbor-blue themed, with an explicit aria-label). This is the affordance that lets the user's Windows build tell us definitively whether the keychain persists. Catch IPC throws so the panel never blanks.

Update frontend tests: any test mounting Settings/Diagnostics or <App/> must mock the new test_key_storage command with a well-formed shape ({ ok, detail }) alongside the existing provider_diagnostics/list_available_models/etc mocks. Add a DiagnosticsSection test asserting the button invokes test_key_storage and renders the result (use await findBy*/waitFor after the async invoke). Ensure Settings sections remain conditionally mounted so section-nav tests assert while the Diagnostics section is mounted.

Run the offline self-audit for this feature (see context.verification_instructions): cargo fmt --check on secrets + tauri-app if the toolchain/registry are available; whole-frontend `NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check .`; static review for clippy/eslint/tsc classes. Note in findings what was verified live vs. static-only vs. CI-only.
acceptance_criteria: crates/secrets/Cargo.toml enables a real platform keyring backend per target (windows-native on Windows) with default-features=false, and the manifest comment explains why the mock-store fallback was the bug.
SecretStore has a self_test() that returns Result<(), SecretError> (no plaintext in its signature) and is unit-tested for both success (InMemory) and failure paths.
A unit test proves a store() Err aborts set_cloud_provider_inner/set_local_runtime_inner WITHOUT persisting a ProviderConfig row.

A `test_key_storage` Tauri command exists, is registered in generate_handler!, has a camelCase serde view, a typed IPC wrapper, and a TS type; the Diagnostics section renders a 'Test key storage' result.
Frontend tests mock test_key_storage everywhere Settings/App is mounted, and a DiagnosticsSection test asserts the invoke + rendered result.
`cargo test --manifest-path crates/secrets/Cargo.toml` (InMemory-based tests) passes in CI, and the secrets crate still builds standalone on the CI ubuntu runner.
verification: Run `cargo test --manifest-path crates/secrets/Cargo.toml` and confirm all non-ignored tests pass (if registry/toolchain available; else record CI-only).

Run `cargo build --manifest-path crates/secrets/Cargo.toml` and `--manifest-path crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml` to confirm the feature/command changes resolve (or record CI-only under INTEGRATIONS_ONLY).

From hybrid-orchestrator/frontend run `npm test` (vitest) and confirm the Diagnostics self-test test and all Settings/App tests pass; run `NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check .` clean (or record CI-only if node_modules unavailable).
Confirm behavioral proof path: describe how the user runs 'Test key storage' on their Windows build to confirm Credential Manager persistence.
findings:
IMPLEMENTED. Keyring backend features selected per target in crates/secrets/Cargo.toml (default-features=false, version pinned at 3): Windows -> `windows-native` (Windows Credential Manager); macOS/iOS (cfg(any(target_os=macos, target_os=ios))) -> `apple-native`; Linux/FreeBSD/OpenBSD -> `linux-native` (kernel keyutils). Chose `linux-native` over the DBus sync-secret-service backend BECAUSE keyutils builds AND runs on the headless CI ubuntu runner with NO running Secret Service daemon and NO system libdbus/openssl at build time. VERIFIED LIVE that `cargo build/clippy -D warnings/test --manifest-path crates/secrets/Cargo.toml` all succeed in the sandbox (network to crates.io was actually available): keyring v3.6.3 resolved and pulled linux-keyutils v0.2.5, compiled clean with no dbus. Manifest comment rewritten to explain the mock/no-op fallback was the v0.8.1 bug.

STORE-ERROR ORDERING: CONFIRMED (not changed) already correct in both set_cloud_provider_inner and set_local_runtime_inner in crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs: secret_store.store(...) is called with `?` BEFORE the ProviderConfig upsert (repo.insert/update), so a store() Err aborts before any row is written. No reorder needed. Added FailingSecretStore-based unit tests proving both inner fns surface the store Err as ErrorCode::Internal AND leave no ProviderConfig row (ProviderRepo::get returns None).

SELF-TEST: added `fn self_test(&self) -> Result<(), SecretError>` as a default trait method on SecretStore (stores sentinel under 'harbor-selftest', resolves, asserts equality, deletes; returns Result<(), SecretError> only, never the sentinel -> preserves resolve-is-the-only-plaintext-seam invariant). Unit-tested Ok over InMemory (and cleanup), Err over a non-persisting store (NotFound path == the exact mock-store failure mode), and Err over a value-mismatch store (Backend 'mismatch').

COMMAND + UI: added display-safe `test_key_storage` command (KeyStorageTestView { ok: bool, detail: String }, rename_all camelCase, Serialize) folding SecretError into { ok:false, detail } so the panel never blanks; registered in generate_handler! in crates/tauri-app/src/lib.rs; typed IPC wrapper testKeyStorage() in frontend/src/ipc/commands.ts; KeyStorageTestResult type in frontend/src/types/index.ts; 'Test key storage' button (aria-label, harbor-blue via settings-form, disabled while in flight, IPC catch) in DiagnosticsSection.tsx.

VERIFIED LIVE: secrets crate cargo fmt --check + clippy -D warnings + test (8 pass, 1 ignored keyring round-trip) all green. cargo fmt --check clean for secrets AND tauri-app.

CI-ONLY (could not run in sandbox): (1) tauri-app cargo build/test/clippy - the sandbox rustc is 1.92.0 but transitive AWS SDK deps (aws-credential-types 1.3.0 / aws-sigv4 / aws-smithy-* via the providers bedrock adapter) require rustc >=1.94.1, and no per-crate Cargo.lock is committed to pin older versions; CI uses dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable (>=1.94) so it compiles there. My tauri-app edits are confined to commands.rs (+ lib.rs handler registration) and were static-audited: Serialize imported, ErrorCode::Internal/CommandError::internal/ProviderRepo all present, view is camelCase, sync #[tauri::command] returning a value matches the app_version precedent. (2) ALL frontend gates (vitest/tsc/eslint/prettier) - NO Node/npm/npx toolchain exists in the sandbox at all. Static-audited: prettier printWidth 100 respected in new lines (only pre-existing template-literal/JSX-text lines exceed), double-quotes + semicolons + trailing commas, imports kept alphabetical (KeyStorageTestResult), added test_key_storage mock ({ ok, detail }) to EVERY Settings/App mount path (both diagnostics mockImplementations in settings.test.tsx + routeInvoke in app.test.tsx), new DiagnosticsSection tests use findBy*/waitFor after the async invoke and assert while the (conditionally-mounted) Diagnostics section is active, added a commands.test.ts wrapper test. STATIC-ONLY.

BEHAVIORAL PROOF PATH for the user's Windows build: open Settings -> Diagnostics -> click 'Test key storage'. The button round-trips a sentinel through Windows Credential Manager via the now-enabled windows-native backend. If it renders 'ok: Keychain round-trip succeeded: secrets persist on this system.' the fix is confirmed (previously the mock store silently accepted writes but never persisted, yielding the 'no secret found for handle ...' errors). An 'ok'=false detail would mean the backend still is not persisting. NOTE: the user's separate request (think-trace on/off toggle in the chat bar) is a different Phase-A feature and is intentionally OUT OF SCOPE for FEAT-002 (the keychain fix); it is not touched here.
